title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction and spillover-aware eviction heuristics
author: Marissa Cole
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncoordinated spillover have been a recurring source of degraded latency p99s and increased host paging during high-concurrency workloads. This PR introduces an end-to-end set of changes to reduce fragmentation via adaptive in-place compaction, bias eviction toward low-reuse/fragmented regions, and make eviction decisions spillover-aware so that we prioritize items that reduce host paging and unnecessary I/O. Approach: 1) Adaptive compaction: a background compactor that prioritizes densely-fragmented pages and opportunistically coalesces free slots using a lightweight heuristic that bounds CPU and GPU memory copy overhead. Compaction is rate-limited and slope-aware to avoid disrupting hot-path token service. 2) Spillover-aware eviction scoring: eviction score now combines LRU-ish recency, reuse frequency, fragmentation contribution (how many small holes reclaimable), and an estimated spill cost computed from residency and IO pressure counters. 3) Scheduling changes: the runtime scheduler now tags aggressive compaction windows during observed low-latency slack (between batches) and defers heavy compaction when request latencies approach SLOs. 4) Telemetry + knobs: new metrics exported (compactions/sec, reclaimed_bytes, spill_decisions, estimated_spill_cost) and three new tunables exposed in the config: compaction_rate_limit, spill_cost_threshold, and fragmented_region_threshold. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks show 18-24% reduction in p99 latency under high-concurrency chat workloads and a 35% reduction in host page-ins on models with large KV footprints. Unit tests cover compactor invariants, eviction scoring math, and safe concurrency handoffs. Rollout plan: staged rollout with canary in dedicated clusters, synthetic load gating, and automatic rollback if p99 regressions exceed 10%. See linked Linear tickets for rollout automation changes. Impact and risks: compaction does GPU memory copies which can increase tail latency if not rate-limited — the compaction rate limiter and scheduler workarounds address this. Spill cost estimates are heuristics and may need tuning per workload; default is conservative. This PR is performance-sensitive and includes a runtime flag to disable the adaptive compactor in emergencies.

perf: include benchmark harness for high-concurrency chat workloads
review_comments: Ravi: Can you clarify how compaction interacts with the KV cache lock? Concerned about head-of-line blocking during compaction.

Marissa: Compaction runs using a try-lock and fallbacks to a lightweight background scanner; it never takes the hot-path write lock. Added a diagram in compaction.rs comments and unit tests that assert no blocking on hot insert paths.
Lena: The spill_cost heuristic seems to prefer keeping larger contiguous regions which could unfairly penalize small but hot entries. Can we add a decay factor for reuse frequency?
Marissa: Added reuse_decay parameter and tuned defaults after offline simulations; included as spill_cost_decay in the config and added tests covering edge cases.
Tomás: CI flaky in integration on first run (integration-tests/kv_cache_integration) — looks like a timing issue with compaction scheduling.
Marissa: Fixed race by moving compaction scheduling off the shared tokio runtime into a dedicated low-priority worker pool; reran CI and it passed.
